These are the conditions on one step. The run theorem asks for the appropriate row
again at every fetched instruction; it does not infer their preservation from reset.

H Constructing the quoting operation
The proof in Section 11 uses a program that takes the code of a term and returns the
code of that code. Here is its construction. Nothing in the operation lets a program
inspect itself by magic: its input is an ordinary tree encoded as a closed lambda term.

                                         497
The Thiele Machine                                                            Devon Thiele


H.1 Numerals and syntax as data
For readability, the formulas below give names to bound variables. Renaming a
bound variable changes nothing; the underlying syntax uses the de Bruijn indices
of Definition 11.3. Applications associate to the left. Write X ⇓ Y here for a finite
sequence of the weak call-by-value steps ending in the value Y.

Scott numerals are the following closed values:

                           0 = λz.λs.z,      n + 1 = λz.λs.s n.

Thus a numeral selects either the supplied zero case or the supplied successor case,
passing its predecessor to the latter. The cases below are values, so choosing one does
not prematurely run the other.

The three syntax constructors, operating on already encoded children, are

                                V = λn.λv.λa.λl.v n,
                                A = λp.λq.λv.λa.λl.a p q,
                                L = λp.λv.λa.λl.l p.

For a variable of index n, an application and an abstraction, respectively, define their
codes by the following resulting values:

                               ⌜#n⌝ = λv.λa.λl.v n,
                               ⌜ p q⌝ = λv.λa.λl.a ⌜ p⌝ ⌜q⌝,
                               ⌜λp⌝ = λv.λa.λl.l ⌜ p⌝.

In particular, V n, A ⌜ p⌝ ⌜q⌝ and L ⌜ p⌝ reduce to these three codes. A code is closed
even when the term it describes has a free variable: the index of that variable is stored
as a numeral. It is data inside the code, not a free variable of the code.

H.2 Recursion without running under a lambda
The usual self-application trick has to delay its recursive call in a call-by-value lan-
guage. Use

               W = λx.λ f .λv. f (λa.x x f a) v,     rec( F ) = λv.W W F v.

When F and u are closed values, beta reduction gives

             rec( F ) u −→ W W F u −→∗ F (λa.W W F a) u = F (rec( F )) u.

The recursive argument is a lambda, hence already a value. It starts work only when
F applies it to an argument. That is the whole reason this construction survives the
call-by-value rule.



                                            498
The Thiele Machine                                                                  Devon Thiele


H.3 Quoting numerals
Let Ej = ⌜#j⌝ for j = 0, 1, 2, and let Z = ⌜0⌝, obtained directly from the finite syntax
of 0 = λλ.1. Write Lk ( X ) for k nested applications of the syntax builder L to X; it is an
abbreviation for constructing k lambda nodes, not a new operation of the language.

Define
                FN = λr.λn. n Z (λk.L2 ( A E0 (r k))),           Q N = rec( FN ).

Then Q N n ⇓ ⌜n⌝, by induction on n. At zero the Scott numeral selects Z. At a
successor it passes n to the second case; the induction hypothesis supplies the code of
n, and the builders produce the code of λλ.(#0 n), which is exactly the syntax of n + 1.

H.4 Quoting terms
For a proposed recursive call r, define three handlers:

                               HV = λn.L3 ( A E2 ( Q N n)),
                            H A (r ) = λp.λq.L3 ( A ( A E1 (r p)) (r q)),
                            HL (r ) = λp.L3 ( A E0 (r p)).

Now set
                     FQ = λr.λt.t HV ( H A (r )) ( HL (r )),    Q = rec( FQ ).

The handlers are lambdas and so are values. The Scott code of the input chooses one
of them and hands it the encoded children. Induction on the represented term proves
Q ⌜t⌝ ⇓ ⌜⌜t⌝⌝:

   • For t = #n, the first handler constructs three lambda nodes over an application
     of variable 2 to the quoted numeral. That is the syntax of λλλ.(#2 n), the code of
     #n.
   • For t = p q, the induction hypotheses quote both child codes. The second handler
     constructs three lambdas over variable 1 applied to those two codes. That is the
     syntax of the application code.
   • For t = λp, the last handler constructs three lambdas over variable 0 applied to
     the quoted child code. That is the syntax of the abstraction code.

Each recursive call works on a proper child of the finite input tree, or on a smaller nu-
meral. Each builder takes finitely many beta steps. The induction therefore establishes
termination as well as the value returned.

The mkapp used in Section 11 is the builder A here (not the term called A in that
proof). With Q and that builder written out, its self-referential term has every piece on
the page. The companion names are mk_app_enc, rec_spec, Qn_spec and Q_spe
c (LRecursion.v); the construction above is the argument those names identify.




                                                 499
The Thiele Machine                                                             Devon Thiele



I The two fixed interpreters, in full
Section 24 uses two fixed programs. Their code is part of the construction, so here it
is. Each listing runs on the unbounded instruction semantics in Section 17. Sixteen
registers hold natural numbers. Subtraction stops at zero. Left shift by b multiplies by
2b ; right shift divides by 2b and discards the remainder. AND and OR act on binary
digits.

LOAD_IMM takes a destination and a constant; XFER takes a destination and a source.
Arithmetic and bit instructions take a destination followed by two source-register
indices. JUMP takes an absolute instruction address; JNEZ takes a source-register
index and an absolute address. A taken jump replaces the program counter; otherwise
it advances by one. All listed instructions have declared cost zero, omitted from the
operands. Fetching beyond the listing ends the host run.

I.1 Packing the program
For words a0 , . . . , an−1 choose a positive width w with a j < 2w for every j. Such a
width exists for every finite list. Store

                      n −1
                 C = ∑ a j 2wj ,       fetch(C, w, p) = ⌊C/2wp ⌋ mod 2w .
                      j =0


Fetch is a right shift followed by an AND with 2w − 1. Repeated division by 2w proves
that it returns a p for p < n and zero for p ≥ n. The width condition prevents a word
spilling into its neighbour. Code and width are inputs, so the host listing stays fixed
when the guest program grows.

I.2 The four-register guest
The twelve-instruction guest of Definition 24.4 encodes an instruction as

                       o + 16d + 64s1 + 256s2 + 1024c + 262144v,

where o is the opcode, d, s1 , s2 < 4 are register indices, c < 256 is its declared cost and
v is an immediate natural number. Unused fields are zero. These fields occupy bits
0–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, 10–17 and 18 upward.

different halt instruction.

Host registers 0–3 hold guest registers; 11 and 12 hold the guest ledger and program

To verify one iteration, split it at its branch destinations. Addresses 0–6 fetch the word;
7–22 select the first source register and 23–38 the second. Each two-bit index selects
one of registers 0–3. Addresses 39–40 extract the opcode. Zero takes 41–43 to address


                                           503
The Thiele Machine                                                         Devon Thiele


122 with status one. Successive subtractions at 44, 47, 52, 56, 60, 64, 68, 72, 76, 80,
84 and 89 dispatch the twelve genuine opcodes. Arithmetic results go to register 6;
99–114 writes that result to the destination. A jump writes register 12 directly and
skips its ordinary increment at 115. Addresses 116–120 extract and add the guest cost;
121 returns to address zero.

This proves the block lemma in Theorem 24.7 by direct evaluation: a guest step has
a finite, positive host block with the same new guest fields. No valid opcode takes
the malformed exit at 97–98. The displayed branches also rule out an exit partway
through an ordinary block. Induction on completed blocks supplies both directions of
the correspondence, with a final sentinel block for termination.

I.3 The two-counter guest
Word codes are 0 for halt, 1 for increment counter zero, 2 for increment counter one,
3 + 8t for decrement counter zero and jump to t, and 4 + 8t for the same operation
on counter one. A zero counter stays zero and falls through; a positive counter is
decremented and takes the jump. Halt has no successor. The same packing formula
applies. Fetching outside the program returns zero and therefore halts too.

Registers 11 and 10 hold counters zero and one, register 12 the guest program counter,
and 13 and 14 width and code. Register 9 has the three status values above. Registers
0–8 and 15 are scratch. At the canonical initial boundary the scratch registers, status
and host program counter are zero. The host ledger and all non-register fields are
preserved.

Addresses 0–8 fetch the word and extract its low three bits. Opcode zero takes 9–11 to
the end with halted status. Addresses 12–17 increment counter zero; 18–24 increment
counter one. Addresses 25–35 perform the first decrement: 30–31 is the zero branch,
32–35 the positive branch. Addresses 36–47 do the same for the second counter. Each


                                         505
The Thiele Machine                                                          Devon Thiele


successful block returns to address zero with the specified guest update. Width, code
and non-register fields do not change.

Opcodes 5–7 reach the malformed exit at 58–59. The cleanup block 48–57 is part of
the fixed listing, but no dispatch path from address zero enters it. Correctness at
successive boundaries allows arbitrary scratch contents.

Every non-halting guest step therefore has a finite, positive host block. The halt block
ends the host run. Induction over these blocks proves simulation, and reading a host
run block by block gives the converse. The canonical encoding uses only opcodes 0–4,
so an encoded guest cannot take the malformed exit. This supplies the construction
behind the two-counter correspondence in Section 24.

J Sources and mathematical dependencies
These works identify the principal mathematical dependencies and the intellectual
background named in the book. The definitions, statements and worked exam-
ples remain on its pages. A published result about thermodynamic cost, quantum
correlations or universal computation is not an additional theorem proved by this
manuscript.

The guest recursion construction uses effective computability and counter-machine
simulation. Its diagonal step and cost restoration are given in Section 24; the counter
and lambda references identify the established machinery that makes its evaluator ex-
ecutable. The thermodynamic references do not remove the explicit physical premise
of the heat bound. The environmental-record papers motivate Section 13; they do not
prove this book’s pointer conjecture.
